story_text.value:
It's a new feature I've added to my app Pour Decision.

The idea is:

1. Set an interval on your phone and slip it in your pocket

2. The phone vibrates in your pocket on every interval

3. Condition yourself to have sips when you feel the vibration

Benefits:

- You end up drinking way less in a night than you normally would

- You don't feel like you're moderating cus you're never without a drink

- It's discreet so people you're drinking with won't know you're doing this

This is sort of like a HIIT-timer, but to preserve battery I took another approach. It works by pre-scheduling on-device notifications when you start the timer. iOS allows apps to schedule up to 64 notifications. If you were to set say 5-minute intervals, that covers the next 320 minutes - more than 5 hours. The phone uses no battery in between intervals, and only wakes up the device once every 5 minutes, so battery drain is negligible.

story_text.value: River Road Labs is a small artisanal studio based out of Central NJ. We built this tool to scratch our own itch. As AI video and image capabilities get more sophisticated we found that we struggled at times to find the words to describe the aesthetic style we were shooting (no pun) for. Other times it is good to just have a massive resource of styles and imagery to flip through at random and to let serendipity do the rest. Director's Lookbook lets you type a feeling and get dealt a set of style cards with prompt text to use. No more copying or saving prompts, use the tool. The feeling reader is a small hosted model with a free daily allowance. The MCP server is read only, no auth, no key, it works in Claude as a connector and in Cursor as well. Setup is at directorslookbook.app/mcp. The connector keeps no request text, only daily counts of which tools were called. The tool is free, no login, no account. We welcome feedback on how to make the tool better and what looks are missing! Thanks!

story_text.value:
I made a virtual microscope slide for your terminal (inspired by asciiquarium and cbonsai). Cells divide, immune cells chase bacteria, and bacteriophages occasionally cause trouble. You can try it with:

$ pipx install terminal-cells

$ cells

I'd appreciate any suggestions for additional animations to add, especially entities or events that would be visually distinct given the graphical limitations. Any cell biologists in the house?
